T: No chickens were harmed in the making of this menu.
D: A coop of chickens plan a great escape from a farm before they end up in pies.
P: Serve the pies when Mrs Tweedy fires up the pie machine.
S: Egg quota curried egg and cress sandwiches
Mild curried egg mayo with cress on soft white bread

Soft boiled eggs mashed with mayo, a little curry powder and chives, on buttered white bread with crunchy cress, cut into triangles. Boil 6 eggs for 9 minutes, cool in iced water and peel. Mash with 4 tbsp mayo, half a tsp mild curry powder, chopped chives, salt and white pepper. Butter 8 slices soft white bread and spread the egg over 4. Scatter with a punnet of cress, close, cut off the crusts and cut each into 4 triangles.
the rats who trade smuggled goods for eggs

Sharp cheddar, sliced ham and Scotch eggs on a board with water crackers, pickled onions, apple chutney and crisp apple wedges. Simmer 4 eggs for 6 minutes, cool and peel. Wrap each in 100g sausage meat, roll in flour, beaten egg and breadcrumbs and fry at 170C for 6 minutes, then halve. Lay out 250g sharp cheddar in wedges, 150g sliced ham, a packet of water crackers, a small jar of pickled onions, a jar of apple chutney and 2 apples cut into wedges.
Twisted puff pastry with parmesan and paprika, baked crisp
Puff pastry brushed with egg, covered in parmesan and paprika, cut into strips and twisted like yarn, baked at 200C for 12 minutes.
M: Pie machine beef and onion pies
Slow braised beef and onion in Worcestershire gravy, baked in shortcrust

Beef chuck braised with onion, thyme and rich gravy until falling apart, baked in shortcrust with a flaky puff lid, served with mushy peas. No chicken, ever. Brown 1kg diced beef chuck in batches. Add 2 sliced onions, thyme, 2 tbsp tomato paste, 1 tbsp Worcestershire and 500ml beef stock, cover and braise for 2.5 hours. Thicken with 2 tbsp cornflour in water and cool. Line 4 pie tins with shortcrust, fill, top with puff, egg wash and bake at 200C for 30 minutes. Simmer 300g frozen peas with butter and mash roughly.
Leek, mushroom and cheddar farm pie
the Tweedys' Yorkshire farm, no chickens harmed

Leek, mushroom and potato in a creamy sharp cheddar and mustard sauce, baked under golden puff pastry with buttered peas alongside. Boil 500g diced potato for 8 minutes and drain. Soften 2 sliced leeks and 300g sliced mushrooms in 40g butter. Stir in 2 tbsp plain flour, then 400ml milk and cook until thick. Add 150g grated cheddar, 1 tbsp wholegrain mustard and the potato. Tip into a pie dish, top with a sheet of puff pastry, brush with egg and bake at 200C for 30 minutes. Serve with 300g buttered peas.
W: Baked roll of soft dough and raspberry jam, served with custard
Suet or butter pastry spread with raspberry jam, rolled up, wrapped loosely in paper and foil, baked at 180C for 40 minutes. Custard.
K: Coop meeting honey malt hot chocolate
Hot milk with cocoa, malt powder and honey, topped with cream and dark chocolate

Hot milk whisked with dark cocoa, malt powder and honey until frothy, topped with whipped cream and a dusting of grated chocolate. Warm 1L milk in a saucepan until steaming but not boiling. Whisk in 3 tbsp cocoa, 4 tbsp malted milk powder and 2 tbsp honey until smooth and frothy. Pour into four mugs, top each with a spoonful of whipped cream and grate a little dark chocolate over the top.
